title: Linear descent across localization of an algebra sheaf
statement: Let C be an essentially small site and let its abelian sheaves carry the tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let R,T,A,B be commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], phi:R→T and t:1→R. Suppose jR:R→A and jT:T→B exhibit the universal commutative ring localizations at t and phi(t), respectively: multiplication by the image of the section is invertible, and every commutative ring map inverting that section factors uniquely. Let psi:A→B satisfy psi jR = jT phi. For every internal A-module N [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and R-linear map f:Res_phi T→Res_jR N [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], there exists a unique A-linear map g:Res_psi B→N whose underlying abelian sheaf map satisfies g jT=f. There is no basis, finiteness or torsion-freeness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0EMD (lemma-simple-invert-module), module localization universal property, with Tag 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert) to identify arbitrary ring localizations.

proof.text: Replace the essentially small site by a small equivalent site in the coefficient universe, and transport the tensor, ring objects and module objects along its sheaf equivalence. Reconstruct section rings and sectionwise modules using the monoidal sheafification adjunction and [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Multiplication by a global section is invertible if and only if that section has a compatible inverse: apply its inverse endomorphism to the unit. This also shows that its action on every module is invertible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ring-localization-sheafification] to R and T. Their universal properties identify A and B uniquely with the sheafifications of the sectionwise localizations at t and phi(t). The scalar square identifies the two images of t. In particular, the restricted R-module underlying N has invertible t-action. No assertion that sections of a localization sheaf are sectionwise localizations is used.

proof.text: Extend the R-linear map f:T→N on each object to fractions u/phi(t)^n by sending them to jR(t)^(-n) f(u). This is well-defined: a further power killing the cross-multiplied difference of two representatives acts invertibly on N. Apply the ordinary module localization universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Uniqueness on u/1 makes the maps commute with restriction. Sheafification extends them uniquely to an R-linear map B→N.

proof.text: The resulting map is A-linear. Sections of A and B are locally fractions r/t^m and u/phi(t)^n by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. On these representatives A-linearity is the identity jR(t)^(-n-m) f(phi(r)u) = jR(r) jR(t)^(-n-m) f(u), which follows from R-linearity. Separatedness proves the equality globally. Uniqueness in sectionwise module localization and sheafification gives uniqueness among A-linear maps. Transport back along the equivalence of sites. The argument uses killing powers and invertible action, so covers t=0, nilpotent t and zero rings or modules.

theorem sheaf_localization_linearDescent
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory (Sheaf J Ab.{w}) :=
      (sfbSheafTensorStructure (A := Ab.{w}) J).monoidal
    letI : BraidedCategory (Sheaf J Ab.{w}) :=
      (sfbSheafTensorStructure (A := Ab.{w}) J).symmetric.toBraidedCategory
    ∀ (R T A B : Sheaf J Ab.{w})
      [MonObj R] [MonObj T] [MonObj A] [MonObj B]
      [IsCommMonObj R] [IsCommMonObj T] [IsCommMonObj A] [IsCommMonObj B]
      (φ : Mon.mk R ⟶ Mon.mk T) (t : 𝟙_ (Sheaf J Ab.{w}) ⟶ R)
      (jR : Mon.mk R ⟶ Mon.mk A) (jT : Mon.mk T ⟶ Mon.mk B)
      (ψ : Mon.mk A ⟶ Mon.mk B),
      jR ≫ ψ = φ ≫ jT →
      IsIso ((λ_ A).inv ≫ (t ≫ jR.hom) ▷ A ≫ μ[A]) →
      (∀ (D : Sheaf J Ab.{w}) [MonObj D] [IsCommMonObj D]
        (f : Mon.mk R ⟶ Mon.mk D),
        IsIso ((λ_ D).inv ≫ (t ≫ f.hom) ▷ D ≫ μ[D]) →
        ∃! g : Mon.mk A ⟶ Mon.mk D, jR ≫ g = f) →
      IsIso ((λ_ B).inv ≫ (t ≫ φ.hom ≫ jT.hom) ▷ B ≫ μ[B]) →
      (∀ (D : Sheaf J Ab.{w}) [MonObj D] [IsCommMonObj D]
        (f : Mon.mk T ⟶ Mon.mk D),
        IsIso ((λ_ D).inv ≫ (t ≫ φ.hom ≫ f.hom) ▷ D ≫ μ[D]) →
        ∃! g : Mon.mk B ⟶ Mon.mk D, jT ≫ g = f) →
      ∀ (N : Mod (Sheaf J Ab.{w}) A)
        (f : (comap φ.hom).obj (regular T) ⟶ (comap jR.hom).obj N),
        ∃! g : (comap ψ.hom).obj (regular B) ⟶ N,
          jT.hom ≫ g.hom = f.hom
